subject: What should the trial help you learn by 2am?
preheader: Four practical questions for a bed or mattress trial at home.
intro: A showroom assessment can give you a useful first impression of a bed or mattress.
The questions often change once the equipment is used through an ordinary night at home.
sectionTitle: Start with the decision, not the product
body: Before arranging a trial, it can help to define what the trial needs to clarify. That keeps the equipment discussion connected to the person's actual routine and the clinician's judgement.
The relevant observations might include settling, repositioning, returning from the bathroom or getting up in the morning. They will be different for every person.
questions: What decision should the trial help you make?
Which known concerns need observation through ordinary use?
Which tasks are difficult in the current setup?
What observations would help you judge suitability?
actionText: Sleep Choice can help configure and coordinate an in-home trial around the equipment question you are trying to resolve. You do not need to have selected the exact product first.
boundary: A home trial supports the equipment discussion. It does not replace clinical assessment or guarantee suitability, improved sleep or a clinical outcome.
trialFooterText: Seven-night in-home trial availability, service area, equipment configuration and individual arrangements are confirmed per case.
